systems.name: Apache Tika
systems.description: Broad content detection and text/metadata extraction across heterogeneous document and binary formats.

systems.name: Soufflé
systems.description: Datalog system specialized for high-performance recursive relational and static-analysis workloads.

systems.name: Roslyn
systems.description: Compiler APIs exposing C# and Visual Basic syntax, symbols, binding, semantic models, diagnostics, and code transformations.

systems.name: Tree-sitter
systems.description: Incremental, error-tolerant concrete syntax parsing designed for source files that may be incomplete or changing.

systems.name: CUE
systems.description: Constraint/unification language that combines configuration values, schemas, defaults, validation, and composition.

systems.name: Pandoc
systems.description: Structured document conversion engine spanning many markup, publishing, and document formats.

triggers.smell: I am accumulating one parser per incoming file type.
triggers.description: Unknown or mixed document/binary formats must be normalized into text and metadata.
positive_signals: format coverage matters more than pixel-perfect layout
negative_signals: exact visual layout reconstruction is the primary requirement

triggers.smell: I have a work queue that propagates facts until nothing changes.
triggers.description: The core computation is monotone recursive relational propagation or transitive closure.

triggers.smell: I need to know what C# code means, not merely how it parses.
triggers.description: Analysis requires binding, overload resolution, symbols, inferred types, diagnostics, or compiler-faithful refactoring.
negative_signals: only concrete syntax structure is needed
the language is not C# or Visual Basic

triggers.smell: I need syntax trees while source is incomplete, malformed, or changing interactively.
triggers.description: The core need is incremental and error-tolerant concrete syntax across one or more programming languages.

triggers.smell: Configuration is turning into schema + defaults + overlays + custom validation code.
triggers.description: Configuration composition and validation are becoming a constraint system in disguise.
negative_signals: a conventional schema already expresses every required rule cleanly

triggers.smell: I am writing pairwise converters among documentation and publishing formats.
triggers.description: The need is structured conversion among markup, office, publishing, or ebook formats rather than extraction from arbitrary binaries.
negative_signals: the primary need is arbitrary binary content extraction

evidence.title: Crossing-Cost Advantage Atlas: Where Specialist Ecosystems Actually Earn the Boundary

recommendations.advantage: Deletes a large parser-integration subsystem by presenting broad document detection, text extraction, and metadata normalization behind one surface.
avoid_when: The corpus is one narrow well-supported format.
Exact page geometry or rendering fidelity is the actual product requirement.

closest_alternatives.name: format-specific host-language libraries
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer them when format scope is narrow and fidelity requirements are specific.

boundary.interface: Tika app/server or a tiny JBang/JVM wrapper
boundary.notes: Borrow the capability without making the whole application a Java application.

recommendations.example: Normalize a corpus containing PDFs, Office files, email containers, EPUB, archives, and metadata-heavy binaries into searchable text/metadata.

recommendations.advantage: Turns recursive fixed-point propagation into declarative Datalog and supplies optimized evaluation/indexing machinery instead of hand-maintained worklists.
avoid_when: Execution order and side effects are central to correctness.
The workload is dominated by numerical kernels rather than relations.

closest_alternatives.name: imperative worklist algorithm
closest_alternatives.reason: Keep it when the relation set is tiny or operational ordering itself is the point.

closest_alternatives.name: general database recursive CTEs
closest_alternatives.reason: Useful when the analysis already naturally lives inside an RDBMS and performance/expressiveness is sufficient.

boundary.interface: facts in / relations out, or compile to a generated executable

recommendations.example: Express whole-program reachability or taint propagation as recursive relations instead of queues, visited sets, and convergence loops.

recommendations.advantage: Uses the compiler's own semantic model for binding, symbols, overload resolution, diagnostics, and transformations instead of approximating C# meaning.
avoid_when: The target language is outside Roslyn's compiler surface.

closest_alternatives.name: Tree-sitter
closest_alternatives.reason: Excellent for syntax, but deliberately does not provide C# compiler semantics.

boundary.interface: small .NET worker or direct library when the host is already .NET

recommendations.example: Refactor symbol usages correctly across aliases, generics, overloads, inferred types, and partial classes.

recommendations.advantage: Provides incremental, error-tolerant syntax trees across many languages and is designed for interactive source that may not currently compile.
avoid_when: Compiler-faithful symbol binding or type semantics are required.

closest_alternatives.name: Roslyn
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when actual C#/VB compiler semantics matter more than cross-language incremental syntax.

recommendations.example: Maintain syntax trees for a multi-language editor while users are halfway through typing invalid code.

recommendations.advantage: Collapses values, schemas, defaults, validation, and composition into one constraint/unification representation.
avoid_when: Configuration is flat, static, and already well-served by a conventional schema.
Introducing a new DSL costs more than the duplicated validation logic.

closest_alternatives.name: JSON Schema + templating/overlay system
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer when validation is the only nontrivial concern and composition semantics remain simple.

boundary.interface: cue vet/export at build or configuration-generation time

recommendations.example: Replace YAML overlays plus defaults plus schema validation plus bespoke cross-field checks with a single constrained configuration model.

recommendations.advantage: Normalizes many structured document dialects through a common document AST, avoiding a matrix of pairwise converters.
avoid_when: Required conversion fidelity is outside Pandoc's supported semantics.
The problem is extraction from arbitrary binary formats rather than structured conversion.

closest_alternatives.name: Apache Tika
closest_alternatives.reason: Prefer for broad content extraction/metadata normalization rather than format-to-format publishing conversion.

boundary.notes: This is usually not a reason to adopt Haskell.

recommendations.example: Convert Markdown, reStructuredText, LaTeX, HTML, DOCX, or EPUB through one maintained conversion engine.

experiments.title: Hostile mixed-format document corpus
experiments.hypothesis: Tika materially increases successful extraction coverage while reducing format-specific integration code.
success_criteria: Higher format coverage on the same corpus

experiments.title: Recursive analysis bake-off
experiments.hypothesis: Soufflé reduces implementation complexity for monotone recursive analyses without unacceptable performance cost.

experiments.title: Constraint-oriented configuration bake-off
experiments.hypothesis: CUE can replace a multi-layer schema/default/overlay/validation stack with a simpler single representation.
